stories.subject: Summer Walker / Interscope Records contract lawsuit
stories.headline: SUMMER WALKER SUED
stories.deck: Interscope says the singer still owes two albums and an EP after she invoked California’s seven-year rule. The label is seeking damages that could top $50 million; Walker says she will defend her position.
stories.verification: Complex and Rolling Stone independently report the Los Angeles filing, the seven-year-rule dispute, the alleged remaining deliverables, and the potential damages.

stories.subject: Chief Keef / Cole Bennett documentary
stories.headline: SOSA DOC SETS 2027 TARGET
stories.deck: Cole Bennett says the Chief Keef documentary is being made carefully and should arrive in 2027. The film will trace the Chicago drill icon’s rise, hiatus and return, with Kenya Barris’ company attached.
stories.verification: Complex reports Bennett’s October 10, 2026 2027 release-window update; Hypebeast’s Variety-sourced announcement confirms Bennett’s direction and Barris’ production partnership.

stories.subject: Tobe Nwigwe / The Bridge album
stories.headline: TOBE BUILDS THE BRIDGE
stories.deck: The Houston rapper’s 12-track album connects his Texas upbringing with Nigerian roots and opens with Busta Rhymes on “CHINEKE.” Sia, Scarface, Paul Wall and Fat Nwigwe join the cross-cultural release.
stories.verification: Complex and Rolling Stone Africa both report the October 9 release, the Houston/Nigeria concept, the 12-track format, and the Busta Rhymes collaboration.

stories.subject: Jay-Z / Ye / Chris Martin “Big Brother” response
stories.headline: JAY-Z ANSWERS YE
stories.deck: On the finale of his HBO conversation series, Jay-Z rejected Ye’s old “Big Brother” complaint about Chris Martin. He said Martin was already his friend and that artists do not own one another.
stories.verification: Complex and AOL independently report Jay-Z’s episode-seven comments, the Chris Martin collaboration timeline, and the “we don’t own people” framing.

stories.subject: Usher and Chris Brown / R&B Tour cancellations
stories.headline: USHER + BROWN DROP FOUR DATES
stories.deck: The R&B Tour canceled Baltimore, Cincinnati, Columbia and Indianapolis dates while Chris Brown prepares for an October 26 UK sentencing hearing. The promoter cited the demands of a long stadium run, with Atlanta shows still scheduled.
stories.verification: Complex reports the four cancellations and promoter statement; Lucas Oil Stadium’s official announcement independently confirms Indianapolis as a previously scheduled R&B Tour date.

source_policy: At least two current reputable sources per story; five distinct stories; no stale or repeated topics from prior batches or the Oct. 10 08:00 slate.
